The $4000 per 1000 views strategy

Hey


If you've ever looked at a completely boring YouTube channel and thought "wait, how is this thing making money?", this one's for you.


Because it turns out, some of the most unsexy, unglamorous channels on the platform are quietly pulling in six figures a year. 


And they're doing it without going viral, without a massive following, and without doing anything that looks remotely exciting from the outside.


Here's what's actually happening.


A car detailing channel called Detail Geek pulls in anywhere from $13,000 to $38,000 a month just from AdSense.


A lockpicking channel called Lock Noob made $19,000 from a single video. 


And a children's storytelling channel called Story Time at Anie's House is estimated to bring in $7,000 to $20,000 a month in ad revenue, on top of a book deal with Harper Collins and her own Amazon store. 


None of these are massive viral channels with millions of subscribers. 


They're niche, they're consistent, and they're really well-monetized.


And here's the thing they all have in common - but a lot of people completely miss: 


AdSense is just where the money starts, not where it stops.


The creators who are actually building solid six-figure income on YouTube aren't doing it by chasing views. 


They're monetizing on the back end - anything like: 

  • selling their own products

  • building affiliate revenue

  • landing brand deals

  • creating offers that turn their audience into paying customers. 

The channel with the most views is almost never the one making the most money.


Here's a quick way to see just how big that gap is. 


A typical mass market YouTube channel might earn around $20 per 1,000 views from AdSense. 


A properly monetized channel in the right niche can clear $400 or more per 1,000 views once back-end income is factored in. 


And a tightly focused channel built around a business audience? 


That number can go well past $4,000 per 1,000 views. 


The only real difference is whether you've got a monetization system working behind your content, or whether you're just sitting around waiting on ad checks that never seem to be enough.


In this week's video, I walked through five specific channel types that are doing this quietly and consistently, including exactly what they're selling, how they set it up, and why each format works so well.


Watch the full breakdown here.



Talk soon, 

Shane
